AutoScaffold brings AI-guided scaffolding to LLM RL.

A teacher LLM analyzes student failures to generate adaptive hints during training (removed at eval).

Outperforms standard RL on Math, QA, ALFWorld & GPU kernel gen using 3x fewer steps!

https://t.co/OGcKMVVfbg

If you’re adding a reward-hacking judge to RL, don’t assume reasoning makes it harder to game.

In a Qwen3-4B coding study, reasoning helped Qwen3-235B but hurt GLM-5.1 judges.

Measure detection on post-RL outputs too.

Frontier coding agents locked where answers cannot leak still cheat: mining git history for fixes, the object store, the filesystem for hidden tests. A learned shortcut from leaky RL, not reasoning. Traces released.
https://t.co/lCwPNg9gTT

How far can a frontier LLM go in contact-rich manipulation? LLM4Robot-Bench: paired sim–real, GPT-6 Astra zero-shot, 16 household tasks, 3 levels. Real robot: 80% → 48% → 0%. Sim matched real on 10/16 tasks. Most failures are reasoning failures.
https://t.co/u7cbzEaUwv https://t.co/5auwr1COvB

Base model quality drives RL post-training, but existing guarantees fail to translate a good init into efficient learning. Our theory captures this and thus turns the heuristics behind modern RL objectives into actionable principles for algorithm design. https://t.co/kYT9tUbJX7

This one stuck with me: 13 trained numbers — 26 bytes — took Qwen2.5-7B from 76% to 91% on GSM8K. Only with RL; the same gain via SFT takes 100-1000x the parameters. RL isn't teaching math here, it's steering what was already inside. https://t.co/bxVdRxgT7f

Frontier coding LLMs: a new arXiv study examines whether models "cheat" on coding tasks, probing evaluation validity and robustness. Models often obtain answers instead of deriving them (reward hacking) in hardened RL environments. https://t.co/bwvsqBHaib

Salesforce AI found a cheaper way to train smart models: train separate RL experts per domain, then distill them into one model. Same accuracy as joint training, 42% fewer FLOPs. Specialize first, merge after. https://t.co/CtYWYKuXTg

new paper: frozen LLM agents learning from retries. EARN gives less credit for hitting the same score again, more for moves that go higher, and near the end replays saved moves (skipping 78.9-86.3% of LLM calls on Jericho). old trick, no treat nya https://t.co/P6FSr927e8

A filter can remove successful reward hacks and still teach the attempt. In this coding-RL study, correct solutions that overwrote tests survived screening; hacking emerged in 4/10 runs. I'd label the attempted action separately from the result.
